Independent endpoint algebra and full-matrix exact test cases with 1≤q≤p≤4
correctness.rationale: Connectivity and B>0 give positive definiteness on the whole feasible simplex. The log determinant has strictly negative second derivative in every nonzero gain direction, since it is minus the squared Frobenius norm of the conjugated diagonal direction. Thus the optimizer is unique; within-class permutation invariance forces common gains without imposing a restriction. The two zero-sum class subspaces and the constant-vector two-by-two block give the stated determinant even for a singleton class. On the budget line b=(B−pa)/(tq), the endpoint derivatives simplify to pQ(t)/[Bq(B+pqt)] and R(t)/[Bt(B+pq)], where R(t)=p²(B+q)t−(B+p)(B+pq). The denominators are positive. Q has a unique positive zero when B<q² and strictly positive values for all t>0 when B≥q², including B=q². Strict decrease of the derivative makes t_lo<t_hi, gives a unique interior root between the thresholds, and puts each threshold equality at its indicated endpoint. At t=1, Q(1)=B[B+q(p+1−q)]>0 and R(1)=B[p(p−q−1)−B], giving the inclusive cutoff and star corollary. Independently checking the endpoint expressions and matrix decomposition reproduces the example; a separate symbolic and exact finite comparison confirmed the identities and 30 full-matrix determinant cases. No finite check is used to infer an unrestricted parameter theorem.
residual_risks: No independent rerun of the uploaded 6682-check suite; the proof and bounded independent comparisons address the decisive identities. No claim for nonunit bipartite edges, arbitrary vertexwise prices, or integer selection.

evidence: Khosoussi et al. give log-determinant design over affine constraints, including a continuous relaxation, but no two-price shunt phase diagram in the material checked. Joshi–Boyd discuss sensor frequencies and D-optimality in generic design.

The indexed D-optimal thresholds concern deleting rungs of a Möbius ladder or deleting a priced perfect matching among the original edges of K_{n,n}, not grounding either whole vertex class on a fixed K_{p,q}.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A generic optimization formulation determines how to pose the problem but does not give its exact support partition. Fixing all base bipartite edges and varying shunts gives a different reduced Laplacian variation than redistributing edge conductance within the original graph.

evidence: The established formulation yields log-det optimization and generic first order conditions. To get the present thresholds one still needs the two-block decomposition, the actual signed rational endpoint identities, the budget-dependent root count of Q, and the strict ordering of the two cutoffs.

With the same two-price graph in ebfcf6b0163e, the E-optimal transition is stated in terms of target rate p(1−√(α/β)); the A-optimal expressions for K_{2,q} and stars have cubic support conditions and can reactivate hubs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A direct implication would require an objective-specific support theorem or explicit solution for the same Laplacian family. Neither generic tractability nor a deletion formula with different shunts or objectives establishes the stated classification.

evidence: Adding a virtual ground vertex makes L+diag(g) the reduced Laplacian. With cost c_i, π_i=c_i g_i/B and candidate shunt scale B/c_i, the budget becomes ∑π_i=1 and the exact objective has the MAXDET form (P2), regardless of the optimization semantics of discrete edge selection. The forest identity gives another equivalent determinant interpretation.

The indexed K_{p,q} pinning result uses exactly these gain variables and price classes, but maximizes λ_min rather than the product of eigenvalues. The A-optimal analogues minimize a sum of inverse eigenvalues.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The determinant and virtual-ground formulations are equivalent and credited. The smallest eigenvalue and trace inverse are not equivalent objectives, and their different thresholds cannot be reused as determinant thresholds.

originality.rationale: The checked work covers the D-optimal framework, continuous determinant design, and several closely matching models with other objectives or differently assigned conductances. The explicit support diagram for unrestricted grounding on unit K_{p,q}, including both price thresholds, the disappearance of the low-price regime at B=q², and the equal-price budget cutoff, was not covered by the checked specific statements or their immediate implications. No originality is assigned to generic log-det concavity, symmetrization, tree-count interpretation, or standard endpoint optimality criteria.
residual_risks: A bounded search and targeted primary excerpts cannot exclude a different published derivation of the K_{p,q} shunt support thresholds under virtual-ground terminology. Date labels were not used to infer priority.

value.rationale: The exact thresholds locate where a whole class goes unsupported in a natural determinant design over all independent gains. They distinguish small-budget two-sided support transitions from the high-budget disappearance of the low-price endpoint, and give a usable equal-price budget rule for stars and other unbalanced bipartite networks. This class-level support information is not supplied by an optimization routine or by analogous trace-inverse or eigenvalue designs.
residual_risks: The result is model-specific; the interior optimum is specified by a scalar root and no cross-graph design rule is claimed.
